title: The birth of photography
subject: art
description: In **1839**, several inventors finally found how to attach an image to a plate. In less than a century, photography has changed the way we see, remember and believe.

hero.hook: How a chemical invention stole painting's monopoly on reality.

blocks.text: For centuries, artists have used the [[darkroom]]: a dark box that projects the outside world onto a wall. The problem remains the same: the image disappears as soon as you turn off the light. In **1839**, photography was officially born. It is not the work of a single genius, but a race between French and British inventors.
In less than a century, this process freed painting from its role as a document and became the first mass media. It changes our relationship to time, memory and visual truth.

It all starts with **Nicéphore Niépce**, French inventor. Around **1826-1827**, he fixes the first permanent image: *View from the window of Gras*. He coats a tin plate with , a tar that hardens in light. The exposure lasts approximately **8 hours**: the sun has time to illuminate both sides of the buildings. [[Bitumen of Judea]]

blocks.caption: The oldest known photograph, taken by Niépce from his window.

blocks.text: In this image, the shadows of the two facades are visible at the same time: the shooting lasted so long that the sun circled the sky.

After Niépce's death, his associate **Louis Daguerre** discovered the effect of iodine and mercury vapors on silver. He developed the **daguerreotype**, presented to the Academy of Sciences in **1839**. In England, **William Fox Talbot** simultaneously developed the [[The calotype of William Fox Talbot]], which made it possible to make several copies from a negative.

sections.title: The portrait for all, the proof for all

blocks.text: From the years **1840**, photography left the laboratories. Until then, having your portrait was a luxury reserved for those who could pay a painter. With the studios and the [[Carte-de-visite]], a small, inexpensive format, the bourgeoisie and then the working classes gained access to the image of themselves.

blocks.caption: The daguerreotype: a unique image, in striking detail, on silver plate.

blocks.text: The photo also becomes proof. During the Crimean War (**1855**), **Roger Fenton** reports images from the front. During the American Civil War, **Matthew Brady** photographed soldiers and battlefields. The event is no longer just told: it is shown.

If a machine copies a face better than a painter, what use is paint anymore? It’s: figurative art is losing its monopoly on reality. Freed from this duty, the artists explore something else: the sensation of light with the [[The impact of photography on figurative painting]], then the deformation of shapes with the . [[Impressionism]] [[Cubism]]
Photography is gradually claiming its own language: framing, light, moment. It is no longer a simple copy of the world. It becomes an art in its own right.

At the end of the 19th century, George Eastman, founder of Kodak, replaced heavy glass plates with flexible film. The device becomes portable. The slogan “You press the button, we do the rest” marks the birth of the amateur. The family album and the global report are born together.
